historical_source_fields.claim_quote: \paren {j + 2} \paren {r - j + 2} \dbinom r {j + 2} \paren {\paren {j + 1} \paren {n - j} \dbinom s {n - j} + \dbinom s {n - j - 1} \paren {n r - \paren {r + s} \paren {j + 1} } }
historical_source_fields.explanation: The flagged assertion is that the local equality C(r, j+1) = (j+2)(r-j+2) C(r, j+2), implicitly used when line 0052 becomes line 0055, is false. Because the bracketed sum ((j+1)(n-j)C(s,n-j) + C(s,n-j-1)(nr-(r+s)(j+1))) is carried across unchanged, the two lines agree only if that binomial replacement is value-preserving, so a single pair (r, j) violating it refutes the step. The script evaluates both sides in exact integer arithmetic (math.comb with the k<0 or k>n => 0 convention) over all 14883 pairs with 0 <= r <= 120 and -2 <= j <= 120, and in exact Fraction arithmetic over 4860 generalized-binomial triples. Result: the equality holds on 7502 pairs, but every one of those is degenerate (both sides zero because a binomial is out of range). Among the 7260 non-degenerate pairs (0 <= j+1 and j+2 <= r, both binomials strictly positive), the identity fails on all 7260 — it holds on NONE. The structural reason, consistent with the exhaustive scan: the genuine "Factors of Binomial Coefficient" corollary is (j+2) C(r, j+2) = (r-j-1) C(r, j+1), i.e. C(r, j+1) = [(j+2)/(r-j-1)] C(r, j+2). The proof's multiplier (j+2)(r-j+2) equals the true multiplier (j+2)/(r-j-1) only if (r-j+2)(r-j-1) = 1, which is impossible for integers since with d = r-j >= 2 one has (d+2)(d-1) >= 4. So the proof has turned a division by (r-j-1) into a multiplication by (r-j+2); the step is invalid, not merely unproved. No floats were used anywhere; the search is deterministic and stdlib-only.

This local equality is false.
historical_source_fields.problem:
Title: Summation from k to m of r Choose k by s Choose n-k by nr-(r+s)k

:$\ds \sum_{k \mathop = 0}^m \dbinom r k \dbinom s {n - k} \paren {n r - \paren {r + s} k} = \paren {m + 1} \paren {n - m} \dbinom r {m + 1} \dbinom s {n - m}$
historical_source_fields.witness: Take r = 2, j = 0 (so j+1 = 1, j+2 = 2, both binomials in range and strictly positive). The step from line 0052 to 0055 asserts C(r, j+1) = (j+2)(r-j+2) C(r, j+2). Here the left side is C(2,1) = 2, while the right side is (j+2)(r-j+2)C(2,2) = 2 * 4 * 1 = 8. So the claim says X = Y with X = 2 and Y = 8: 2 != 8, a factor-of-4 discrepancy. Equivalent smaller/other witnesses: r = 3, j = 1 gives C(3,2) = 3 vs (3)(4)C(3,3) = 12; r = 4, j = 1 gives C(4,2) = 6 vs (3)(5)C(4,3) = 60. In the generalized (rational upper index) setting r = -40, j = -1 gives C(r,0) = 1 vs (1)(-37)... = 1480, so the failure is not an artifact of integrality.
